DAMGHANI:v1p155/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r8.claim: The losers are those cheated of themselves and their families on Judgment Day, with their spouses and servants lost to others in Paradise.
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r8.anchor: الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r3.claim: One Qur'anic sense is being cheated of or deprived of one's self and family at the Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r3.anchor: والثاني : الغبن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الزمر : ﴿ قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين ﴾

BURSEVI:v8p65/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p65/r6.claim: The command to worship whatever they wish is a threat and challenge, like the parallel command in Fussilat, and implies anger because they persisted after being forbidden.
BURSEVI:v8p65/r6.anchor: والأمر للتحديد كما في قوله تعالى : {اعملوا ما شئتم}

BURSEVI:v8p65/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65/r7.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v8p65/r7.claim: Al-Irshad says the command displays severe anger: people who ignored prohibitions are told to persist so punishment may overtake them.
BURSEVI:v8p65/r7.anchor: في "الإرشاد" : وفيه من الدلالة على شدة الغضب عليهم

BURSEVI:v8p65/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p65/r8.claim: When polytheists taunted Muhammad that he had lost by rejecting his fathers’ religion, the verse answers that the true losers are those who squander what they need.
BURSEVI:v8p65/r8.anchor: ولما قال المشركون خسرت يا محمد حيث خالفت دين آبائك

BURSEVI:v8p65/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65/r9.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p65/r9.claim: Al-Raghib defines loss as reducing one’s capital; it applies to wealth, status, health, safety, intellect, faith, and reward, with the last being the manifest loss.
BURSEVI:v8p65/r9.anchor: وفي "المفردات" : الخسران انتقاص رأس المال يستعمل في المال والجاه والصحة

BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r1.claim: The relative clause identifies who the losers are; they waste and destroy themselves by misguidance and choosing disbelief.
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r1.anchor: بالضلال واختيار الكفر لها ؛ أي : أضاعوها وأتلفوها إتلاف البضاعة

BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r2.claim: Kashifi paraphrases their loss as going astray within themselves.
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (زيان كردند در نفسهاى خودكه كمراه كشتند)

BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r3.claim: They also lose their families by leading them into misguidance and disbelief; ‘family’ may mean spouses, children, servants, relatives, companions, or all of them.
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r3.anchor: أهليهم} بالضلال واختيار الكفر لهم أيضا أصله

BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r4.claim: On Judgment Day they enter the Fire instead of Paradise, exposing themselves and their families to everlasting torment and irreparable ruin.
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r4.anchor: يوم القيامة} حين يدخلون النار بدل الجنة حيث عرضوهما

BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r5.claim: Kashf al-Asrar calls it manifest loss: they exchanged Paradise for fire and ranks for the lowest depths.
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (بدانيد وآكاه باشيدكه آنست آن زيان هويدا

BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r6.claim: The true loser loses worldly life by following desire, the hereafter by violating prohibitions, and the Lord by turning allegiance to another.
BURSEVI:v8p65#2/r6.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" : الخاسر في الحقيقة من خسر دنياه

QASHANI:39:13-16/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:13-16/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:13-16/r3.claim: The true losers are those attached to anything other than God and thereby veiled from the Real; they squander their souls and spiritual kin, kindred sacred substances in their spiritual world.
QASHANI:39:13-16/r3.anchor: بالحقيقة، الكاملين في الخسران، هم الواقفون مع الغير، المحجوبون عن الحق

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r2.claim: The warning to worship as one chooses is the utmost threat; the true loser sacrifices worldly life to desire, the afterlife by disobedience, and his relationship with his Master through shamelessness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r2.anchor: هذا غاية الزجر والتهديد ، ثم بين

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r3.claim: Hell's enclosure keeps its inhabitants from escape or respite; people already dwell in the Hell of their beliefs behind an enduring veil.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r3.anchor: فهم لا يخرجون منها ، ولا يفترون عنها

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r4.claim: Fearing God now protects one from the fear of that Day; otherwise a difficult ascent lies ahead.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r4.anchor: إن خفت اليوم كفيت خوف ذلك اليوم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r1.claim: Qatada says God has prepared a family in Paradise for every person who obeys Him; those who disobey lose themselves and that family.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم ﴾ قال ليس أحد إلا قد أعد الله له أهلا في الجنة إن أطاعه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p171#4/r2.claim: Mujahid gives the same interpretation: obedience would secure the family prepared in Paradise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the order to worship whatever they wish is a threat and an emphatic abandonment of those who have refused faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r4.anchor: والمراد بهذا الأمر الوارد على وجه التخيير المبالغة في الخذلان والتخلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r5.claim: Another view takes the open-ended command as a direct threat, as in the earlier command to enjoy disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: فاعبدوا ما شئتم: صيغة أمر على جهة التهديد لقوله: قل تمتع بكفرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r6.claim: The losers truly lose themselves by becoming Hell's people and lose their families by being separated from them in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r6.anchor: قل إن الخاسرين: أي حقيقة الخسران، الذين خسروا: أي هم الذين خسروا أنفسهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r7.speaker: قتادة وميمون بن مهران
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r7.claim: Qatada and Maymun say God had prepared families for the losers in Paradise, but they lose them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: كأن الله قد أعد لهم أهلا في الجنة فخسروهم، وقال معناه ميمون بن مهران.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r8.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the lost families are the houris.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: هي الحور العين، ثم ذكر ذلك الخسران

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r9.claim: The verse intensifies the warning by naming and emphasizing their unmistakable loss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر ذلك الخسران وبالغ فيه في التنبيه عليه أولا، والإشارة إليه، وتأكيده بالفعل،

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r1.claim: The command to worship whatever they wish conveys intense anger: since they would not stop, they are told to proceed so punishment can come upon them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r1.anchor: وفيه من الدلالة على شدة الغضب عليهم ما لا يخفى كأنهم لما لم ينتهوا عما نهوا عنه أمروا به

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r2.claim: The losers are those fully ruined, having squandered themselves and what they needed to secure.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r2.anchor: أي الكاملين في الخسران وهو إضاعة ما بهم وإترافهم ما لا بد منه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r3.claim: On the main interpretation, their families are followers whom they misled; they ruin themselves and those followers by choosing unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r3.anchor: فالمراد بالأهل أتباعهم الذين أضلوهم أي أضاعوا أنفسهم وأضاعوا أهليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r4.claim: The loss occurs when they enter Hell, having exposed themselves and their followers to everlasting torment.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r4.anchor: حين يدخلون النار حيث عرضوهما للعذاب السرمدي

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r5.claim: Another view takes the Day of Resurrection as the point when their loss becomes manifest and is fully realized.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r5.anchor: ولو أبقى يوم القيامة على ظاهره لأنه يتبين فيه أمرهم ويتحقق مبدأ خسرانهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r6.claim: A further view takes family as followers generally: if they are in Hell, the losers lose themselves; if in Paradise, they are irretrievably separated from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r6.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالأهل الأتباع مطلقا وخسرانهم إياهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that separation from the Paradise-bound would be no meaningful loss if reunion would bring no benefit to the loser.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r7.anchor: وتعقب بأن المحذور ذهاب من لو آب لا ينتفع به الخاسر وذلك غير متصور في الشق الأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r8.speaker: قتادة، مجاهد، ميمون بن مهران
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r8.claim: Qatāda, Mujāhid, and Maymūn ibn Mihrān say everyone has a family prepared in Paradise if they obey God; unbelievers lose that family.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r8.anchor: ليس أحد إلا قد أعد الله تعالى له أهلا في الجنة إن أطاعه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they lose the Paradise-dwellers prepared for them had they obeyed God, thereby depriving those companions too.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r9.anchor: خسروا أهليهم من أهل الجنة كانوا أعدوا لهم لو عملوا بطاعة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r10.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the family as the houris; al-Ālūsī says this reading is somewhat remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r10.anchor: فقد روي عنه أنه فسر الأهل بالحور العين ولا يخفى أن حمل الآية على ذلك لا يخلو عن بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r11.claim: The statement does more than define complete losers: it identifies them as those addressed by the preceding command, either directly or as the foremost members of its category.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251/r11.anchor: بل بيان أنهم المخاطبون بما تقدم إما بجعل الموصول عبارة عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r1.claim: The concluding sentence is independent; its demonstrative marks the loss as remote and immense, while the emphatic pronoun, definite noun, intensive form, and mubīn underscore its totality and horror.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r1.anchor: وتصديرها بحرف التنبيه والإشارة بذلك إلى بعد منزلة المشار إليه في النشر وأنه لعظمه بمنزلة المحسوس

ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r2.claim: The form khusrān is more emphatic than khusr, and describing it as manifest leaves no greater kind of loss beyond it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p251#2/r2.anchor: وتعريف الخسران والإتيان به على فعلان الأبلغ من فعل ووصفه بالمبين من الدلالة على كمال هو له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r2.claim: The losers lose themselves and their families, meaning spouses and servants.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r3.claim: God assigned each person a Paradise home and family; the obedient receive theirs, while a sinner’s home passes to another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r3.anchor: جعل لكل إنسان منزلا في الجنة وأهلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#2/r4.claim: Another view says the self is lost by entering Hell and family by separation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r2.claim: The command to worship whatever they choose besides God is a threat and abandonment of them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r2.anchor: { فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه } تهديدا وخذلانا لهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r3.claim: The complete losers misguide themselves and lead their families astray; on Judgment Day they enter Hell instead of Paradise, combining every kind of loss.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r3.anchor: { الذين خسروا أنفسهم } بالضلال. { وأهليهم } بالإضلال. { يوم القيمة } حين يدخلون النار بدل الجنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r4.claim: They lose family either because their family is in Hell with them or because a family in Paradise is forever separated from them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r4.anchor: وقيل وخسروا أهليهم لأنهم إن كانوا من أهل النار فقد خسروهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r5.claim: The warning is rhetorically intensified by ألا, a resumed sentence, separation, the definite noun for loss, and calling it manifest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:14-15/r5.anchor: مبالغة في خسرانهم لما فيه من الاستئناف والتصدير ب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r3.claim: The invitation to worship whatever they wish is a threat: worshipping anything beneath God risks losing His favor, and no beneficence exists apart from His.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r3.anchor: فإن عبادة ما دونه تؤدي إلى قطع إحسانه , ولا إحسان إلا إحسانه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r4.claim: The losers destroy themselves and their families at the Resurrection; if relatives are damned their loss is shared, and if they are saved there will be no reunion.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r4.anchor: أي لأنهم إن كانوا مثلهم فحالهم في الخسارة كحالهم , ولا يمكن أحدا منهم أن يواسي صاحبه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r5.claim: The Day of Resurrection is the decisive day, when what was lost cannot be repaired.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p431/r5.anchor: لأن ذلك اليوم هو الفيصل لا يمكن لما فات فيه تدارك أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p432/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p432/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p432/r1.claim: The demonstrative phrase identifies this as the uniquely manifest loss; the emphatic form khusrān intensifies its magnitude and reproach.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p432/r1.anchor: أتى بصيغة الفعلان المفهم مطلقا للمبالغة

DURR-FULL:v7p216/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the losers as disbelievers made for the Fire, deprived of worldly life and forbidden Paradise; their lost families are those in Paradise who would have been theirs had they obeyed God.
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم} الآية قال: هم الكفار الذين خلقهم الله للنار

DURR-FULL:v7p216/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r2.claim: Mujahid says they lose themselves through conscious regret in Hell and lose the families to whom they could have returned; Qatada says God prepared a family in Paradise for each person who obeyed Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p216/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم} يخسرونها فيتحسرون في النار أحياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r1.claim: The command to confront the polytheists addresses those who pressed the Prophet to abandon his call and follow their religion; context identifies the two groups addressed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r1.anchor: هذا القول متعين لأن يكون الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمورا بأن يواجه به المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r2.claim: Muqātil reports that Quraysh asked the Prophet what led him to this religion and urged him to follow the faith of his fathers and leaders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم قول مقاتل : قال كفار قريش للنبيء : ما يحملك على هذا الدين الذي أتيتنا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r3.claim: Repeating ‘say’ and the declaration of worshipping God alone reinforces 39:11: the two formulations each imply exclusivity and together establish it three times, preparing the warning that follows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r3.anchor: أمر بأن يعيد التصريح بأنه يعبد الله وحده تأكيدا لقوله : { قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r4.claim: The fāʾ introduces a rhetorical consequence, and ‘worship whatever you wish besides Him’ is a leave-it-to-you challenge showing indifference; their choice rests on whim, not evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p358/r4.anchor: والأمر في قوله : { فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه } مستعمل في معنى التخلية ، ويعبر عنه بالتسوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r1.claim: After the apparent leave-taking, the Qur'an adds admonition indirectly, speaking of the addressees as absent while intending them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r1.anchor: أعقب أمر التسوية في شأنهم بشيء من الموعظة حرصا على إصلاحهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r2.claim: The emphatic opening and definite ‘the losers’ make the phrase a hyperbolic restriction: complete losers are those who lose themselves and their families.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r2.anchor: وافتتح المقول بحرف التوكيد تنبيها على أنه واقع وتعريف { الخاسرين } تعريف الجنس ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r3.claim: The contextual target is the polytheists under debate; the relative clause replaces direct address to warn that they will lose themselves and their families at Judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r3.anchor: علم أن المراد بالذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم هم الذين جرى الجدال معهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r4.claim: Losing oneself pictures people causing their own punishment while imagining they are securing bliss, like a merchant whose capital is ruined; the wording also occurs in 7:9.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p360/r4.anchor: ومعنى خسرانهم أنفسهم : أنهم تسببوا لأنفسهم في العذاب في حين حسبوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r1.claim: They lose their families by leading spouses and children into disbelief, so neither they nor their relatives benefit or help one another in the next life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r1.anchor: وذلك أنهم أغروا أهليهم من أزواجهم وأولادهم بالكفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r2.claim: The concluding ‘that is the manifest loss’ draws the result: losing one's dearest things makes their loss the greatest and clearest, emphasized by the verbal noun al-khusrān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r2.anchor: ولذلك أوثرت خسارتهم باسم الخسران الذي هو اسم مصدر الخسارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r3.claim: The demonstrative, attention particle, and separating pronoun heighten and rhetorically restrict the judgment of their loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p361/r3.anchor: وبتوسط ضمير الفصل المفيد للقصر وهو قصر ادعائي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r5.claim: Worship whatever you wish is a threat, like the commands in the cited verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r5.anchor: وقوله: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه صيغة أمر على جهة التهديد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r6.claim: Losing one's family may mean the family one would have had in Paradise, or one's worldly family lost through punishment; either way a person in Paradise has no true loss.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p524/r6.anchor: لأن قوله: وأهليهم قيل معناه أنهم خسروا الأهل الذي كان يكون لهم لو كانوا من أهل الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r1.claim: Worship whatever you wish is a threat; it is not an operative command that can be abrogated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r1.anchor: وهذا تهديد وبعضهم يقول هو منسوخ بآية السيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r2.claim: One view says the losers lost the houris prepared for them in Paradise had they obeyed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r2.anchor: أحدها أنهم خسروا الحور العين اللواتي أعددن لهم في الجنة لو أطاعوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r3.claim: Another view says they lost their family in Hell because they have no family there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r3.anchor: والثاني خسروا الأهل في النار إذ لا أهل لهم فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r4.claim: A third view says they lost worldly relatives: the disbelievers went to Hell while their believing family went to Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p169#4/r4.anchor: والثالث خسروا أهليهم الذين كانوا في الدنيا إذ صاروا إلى النار بكفرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90/r2.claim: The command to worship as they wish is a threat and declaration of disavowal; the real losers lose themselves and their families at the Resurrection, forever separated without reunion or joy.

JISHUMI:v8p6045#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6045#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6045#2/r7.claim: One report says these verses were revealed when people invited the Messenger to follow his forefathers' religion.
JISHUMI:v8p6045#2/r7.anchor: قيل: لما دعوا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وآله - إلى دين الآباء نزلت هذه الآيات

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r1.claim: They lose themselves in the Fire and families because they find no family there though they once had one in this world.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r1.anchor: خسروا أنفسهم بإهلاكها في النار , وخسروا أهليهم بأن لا يجدوا في النار أهلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r2.claim: They lose themselves by being denied Paradise and their families by losing its prepared houris.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r2.anchor: خسروا أنفسهم بما حرموها من الجنة وأهليهم من الحور العين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r3.claim: They may lose themselves as unbelievers in Hell while believing families enter Paradise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119/r3.anchor: بأن صاروا هم بالكفر إلى النار , وصار أهلوهم بالإيمان إلى الجنة وهو محتمل

MUQATIL:39:11-16/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:11-16/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:11-16/r6.claim: The losers deceive and ruin themselves and lose their spouses and servants on Resurrection Day because they did not affirm God's oneness.
MUQATIL:39:11-16/r6.anchor: { إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا } يعنى غبنوا { أنفسهم } فصاروا إلى النار { وأهليهم } يعنى وخسروا أهليهم من الأزواج والخدم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r1.claim: “Worship what you wish” is a threat; it was revealed when the Prophet was told that abandoning his ancestors' religion would make him a loser.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r1.anchor: وهذا أمر تهديد وقيل له عليه السلام ان خالفت دين آبائك فقد خسرت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r2.claim: The true losers combine every kind of loss: they destroy themselves in the Fire and lose the families they led astray.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r2.anchor: أى الكاملين فى الخسران الجامعين لوجوهه وأسبابه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r3.claim: The warning's rhetoric intensifies the horror through an attention particle, a separator between subject and predicate, a definite noun, and “manifest”; they traded Paradise and ranks for Fire and pits.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p50#5/r3.anchor: حيث صدر الجملة بحرف التنبيه ووسط الفصل بين المبتدا والخبر وعرف الخسران

QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r6.claim: The command to worship whatever one wants is a threat, warning, and rebuke, like another threatening command.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r6.anchor: أمر تهديد ووعيد وتوبيخ كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r7.claim: Another view says the threat was abrogated by the command to fight.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r8.claim: Through Maymūn ibn Mihrān, Ibn ʿAbbās says everyone has a spouse created for them in Paradise, so one who enters Hell loses both self and family.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r8.anchor: قال ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس: ليس من أحد إلا وقد خلق الله له زوجة في الجنة، فإذا دخل النار خسر نفسه وأهله.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r9.claim: Another report says obedience secures that home and family, apart from what the person already possessed, as in the verse on the inheritors.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:11-16/r9.anchor: في رواية عن ابن عباس: فمن عمل بطاعة الله كان له ذلك المنزل والأهل إلا ما كان له قبل ذلك، وهو قوله تعالى:

ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n18/r1.claim: Losing one's self means destruction of one's true human identity and uniqueness, alongside irreversible separation from loved ones at resurrection.
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n18/r1.anchor: the destruction of one's true identity and uniqueness

STUDYQURAN:39:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r1.claim: The opening command is a threat to disbelievers and repudiates them, paralleling verses that disavow partners and the complete separation in Sūrah 109.
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r1.anchor: The first sentence of this verse is both a threat to the disbelievers and a means of repudiating them

STUDYQURAN:39:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r2.claim: The losers have lost this world and the Hereafter by wasting the chance to do good and repent; they lose their families as they will have no one for comfort or commiseration.
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r2.anchor: they have wasted the opportunity to perform righteous deeds and repent in this world

STUDYQURAN:39:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r3.claim: In contrast, the righteous enter Paradise with righteous fathers, spouses, and progeny.
STUDYQURAN:39:15/r3.anchor: they shall enter along with those who were righteous from among their fathers, their spouses, and their progeny

TAB-FULL:v20p181/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p181/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p181/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to declare that he worships God alone with sincere, undivided obedience and disavows all partners and rival gods.
TAB-FULL:v20p181/r1.anchor: الله أعبد مخلصا، مفردا له طاعتي وعبادتي، لا أجعل له في ذلك شريكا

TAB-FULL:v20p181/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p181/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p181/r2.claim: The polytheists may worship whatever they choose among created things, but will learn the outcome when they meet their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v20p181/r2.anchor: فاعبدوا أنتم أيها القوم ما شئتم من الأوثان والأصنام وغير ذلك مما تعبدون

TAB-FULL:v20p182/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r1.claim: The losers are those who perish by God's punishment, losing their families with themselves; in Hell they have no family, though they had families in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r1.anchor: الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v20p182/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the losers are unbelievers destined for Hell, barred from Paradise, and deprived of worldly life; he links this loss to 22:11.
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة} [الزمر: 15] قال: " هم الكفار الذين خلقهم الله للنار

TAB-FULL:v20p182/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they lose themselves in this world and have no family in Hell, although they had families before.
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة} [الزمر: 15] قال: «هؤلاء أهل النار

TAB-FULL:v20p182/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r4.claim: Mujahid says they lose their families with whom they can no longer reunite and lose themselves by perishing in the Fire, dying while still alive.
TAB-FULL:v20p182/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قال: " غبنوا أنفسهم وأهليهم

TABATABAI:39:13-15/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r9.claim: The order to worship whatever they wish besides God is a threat: it will not benefit them, and they will suffer the consequence of turning away.
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r9.anchor: أمر تهديدي بمعنى أنهم لا ينفعهم ذلك فإنهم مصيبهم وبال إعراضهم

TABATABAI:39:13-15/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r10.claim: Loss is the wasting of capital, and khusrān is more emphatic; losing oneself means entering ruin so completely that the capacity for happiness is lost.
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r10.anchor: وخسران النفس هو إيرادها مورد الهلكة والشقاء بحيث يبطل منها استعداد الكمال

TABATABAI:39:13-15/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r11.claim: The idolaters lose themselves through unbelief and their families by leading their close relations into unbelief and associationism.
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r11.anchor: فإنكم تخسرون أنفسكم بإيرادها بالكفر مورد الهلكة وأهليكم وهم خاصتكم بحملهم على الكفر والشرك

TABATABAI:39:13-15/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r12.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r12.claim: Family may mean the spouses and servants God would have prepared for each person in Paradise had they believed; the author finds this more fitting.
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد بالأهل من أعده الله في الجنة للإنسان لو آمن واتقى من أزواج وخدم وغيرهم

TABATABAI:39:13-15/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r13.claim: The Paradise-family reading fits better because worldly kinship and social ties are severed on the Day of Resurrection.
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r13.anchor: فإن النسب وكل رابطة من الروابط الدنيوية الاجتماعية مقطوعة يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:39:13-15/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r14.claim: This is manifest loss because worldly wealth or status loss is temporary and replaceable, while loss of the self is eternal and cannot be replaced.
TABATABAI:39:13-15/r14.anchor: سريع الزوال منقطع الآخر بخلاف خسران يوم القيامة الدائم الخالد فإنه لا زوال له

TABRISI:39:11-20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:11-20/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:11-20/r1.claim: The manifest loss is obvious and cannot be hidden; the phrase echoes the description of inheritors of Paradise.
TABRISI:39:11-20/r1.anchor: أي البين الظاهر الذي لا يخفى

THALABI:v8p226/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p226/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p226/r4.claim: The command to worship whatever one wishes besides God is a reproach and threat, like 41:40; another view says the fighting verse abrogated it.
THALABI:v8p226/r4.anchor: أمر توبيخ وتهديد كقوله اعملوا ما شئتم

THALABI:v8p226/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p226/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p226/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says everyone has a home and family allotted in Paradise; the obedient receive theirs, while the disobedient go to Hell and leave theirs as inheritance to the obedient.
THALABI:v8p226/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن الله تعالى جعل لكل إنسان منزلا في الجنة وأهلا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r1.claim: The losers lose themselves through everlasting residence in Hell and lose their families because they do not join believers' families in Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r1.anchor: { قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم } بالتخليد في النار { وأهليهم }

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r1.claim: The Prophet conveys God's rulings without error and is himself bound to obey them, facing punishment if he acts otherwise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r1.anchor: Peygamber, Allah’ın bildirdiği hükümleri eksiksiz ve yanlışsız duyurduğu gibi, bizzat kendisinin de bu hükümleri yerine getirmekle yükümlü olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r2.claim: The command to worship whatever is chosen besides God is a warning and threat to those who persist in idolatry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r2.anchor: Artık siz de O’nun dışında dilediğinize tapın bakalım!” cümlesi bir uyarı ve tehdit ifadesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r3.claim: The losers lose their own selves through deserved punishment in Hell and lose relatives because they cannot meet or help them there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:15/r3.anchor: Onların âhirette öz benliklerini kaybetmeleri, “cehennemde hak ettikleri cezaya çarptırılmaları”; yakınlarını kaybetmeleri de

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r5.claim: The Prophet publicly disavows polytheism, while its adherents are warned and those committed to monotheism receive glad tidings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r5.anchor: a declaration of acquittal is sounded from the tongue of the Prophet (sws) to polytheism and polytheists.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r5.claim: The Prophet's forceful disavowal of polytheism shows that coercion and oppression cannot make God's servants submit to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r5.anchor: they cannot make God’s servants submit to polytheism through coercion and oppression.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r2.claim: The Prophet declares his acquittal from opponents: he worships and obeys God alone and invites them to this, while they may worship whom they choose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r2.anchor: This in very clear words is a declaration of acquittal and severing of ties by the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r3.claim: The real losers forfeit themselves and their families in the Hereafter; worldly losses are temporary, while this loss is eternal, so sacrificing the next life for brief worldly pleasure is ruinous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r3.anchor: the real losers are the ones who have put themselves and their family in loss on the Day of Judgement

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r4.claim: Adding family to the loss makes each person responsible for seeking their family’s salvation; setting a bad example or leading them astray incurs responsibility for their ruin too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r4.anchor: The following words of the Prophet (sws) explain this fact

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r5.speaker: Prophet (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r5.claim: The Prophet teaches that every person is a shepherd accountable for those under their care.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p537/r5.anchor: The following words of the Prophet (sws) explain this fact

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p538/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p538/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p538/r3.claim: People mistake lost worldly interests for real loss, but the true loss is permanent deprivation in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p538/r3.anchor: in fact, real loss is one whose result is eternal deprivation

NAHHAS:v4p7/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p7/r11.claim: الذين is nominative as the predicate of إن, while أهليهم is accusative, coordinated with أنفسهم and marked by yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r11.anchor: الذين في موضع رفع على خبر إن وأهليهم في موضع نصب معطوفون على أنفسهم

NAHHAS:v4p7/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p7/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p7/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says that God created everyone a spouse in Paradise; one who enters Hell loses himself and his family.
NAHHAS:v4p7/r12.anchor: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس ليس من أحد إلا وقد خلق الله جل وعز له زوجة في الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r1.claim: Rational first principles are capital for reasoning, whose combinations yield acquired knowledge like a trader's investment yields profit; using one's capacities in good works likewise yields profit.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r1.anchor: العلوم البديهية المسماة بالعقل رأس المال وتركيبها على الوجوه المخصوصة يشبه تصرف التاجر

RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r2.claim: A person given life, intellect, and ability who gains neither knowledge of truth nor good deeds loses all capital at death and is wholly ruined.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r2.anchor: إن من أعطاه الله الحياة والعقل والتمكن

RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r3.claim: Disbelievers use their intellect and strength to devise delusions and do evil; their exertion is wasted in life, lost at death, and becomes a cause of punishment afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223#2/r3.anchor: استعملوا عقولهم التي هي رأس مالهم في استخراج وجوه الشبهات وتقوية الجهالات

ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r2.claim: Those who lose themselves have ruined their capacity for arrival and union; their families are their hearts, secrets, and spirits, lost through turning away from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r2.anchor: أي الذين تبين خسران أنفسهم بإفساد استعدادها للوصول والوصال ( وأهليهم ) من القلوب والأسرار والأرواح

ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r3.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r3.claim: An eminent scholar compares knowledge and good works to profits from two kinds of trade; wasting God-given reason, health, and ability leaves a person with lost capital and lasting torment of ignorance and separation.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r3.anchor: إن للإنسان قوتين يستكمل بأحداهما علما وبالأخرى عملا والآلة الواسطة في القسم الأول هي العلوم المسماة بالمقدمات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r10.claim: The command to worship what people wish besides God is a choice-form command that intensifies abandonment and leaves them to their fate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r10.anchor: ولذلك رتب عليه قوله : { فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه } والمراد بهذا الأمر الوارد على وجه التخيير : المبالغة في الخذلان والتخلية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r11.claim: The losers ruin themselves irreversibly and lose their families, whether those families share their fate in Hell or are in Paradise and permanently separated from them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r11.anchor: الذين خسروا أنفسهم } لوقوعها في هلكة لا هلكة بعدها ( و ) خسروا { أهليهم } لأنهم إن كانوا من أهل النار فقد خسروهم كما خسروا أنفسهم ، وإن كانوا من أهل الجنة فقد ذهبوا عنهم ذهابا لا رجوع بعده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r12.claim: An alternative says they lost the families they would have had if they had believed, since they would then have joined believers who have families in Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : وخسروهم لأنهم لم يدخلوا مدخل المؤمنين الذين لهم أهل في الجنة ، يعني : وخسروا أهليهم الذين كانوا يكونون لهم لو آمنوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r13.claim: The phrase ‘manifest loss’ intensifies the description through an independent sentence, an alerting particle, separation between subject and predicate, and a definite noun qualified as manifest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p120#2/r13.anchor: ولقد وصف خسرانهم بغاية الفظاعة في قوله : { ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين } حيث استأنف الجملة وصدرها بحرف التنبيه ، ووسط الفصل بين المبتدأ والخبر

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r2.claim: “Worship whatever you wish apart from Him” is a rebuke after the case for monotheism is complete, not a genuine command.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r2.anchor: فبعد ذلك أنتم أعرف بأنفسكم ، ثم بين تعالى كمال الزجر بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r3.claim: The losers lose themselves by falling into the greatest conceivable ruin and lose their families as well.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r3.anchor: لوقوعها في هلاك لا يعقل هلاك أعظم منه ، وخسروا أهليهم أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r4.claim: They lose their families either because those families enter Hell too, or because saved families are forever separated from them.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r4.anchor: وإن كانوا من أهل الجنة ، فقد ذهبوا عنهم ذهابا لا رجوع بعده ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that each man has a home, family, and servants in Paradise; if he obeys he receives them, but otherwise loses them and Muslims inherit them.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : إن لكل رجل

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r6.claim: The lexical sense of خسِر is to be cheated or defrauded.

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r7.claim: The repetition emphasizes the gravity of the loss.

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r8.claim: The opening particle ألا alerts listeners and signals that the matter is too great for their minds to encompass.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r8.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر في أول هذه الكلمة حرف ألا وهو للتنبيه ، وذكر التنبيه في هذا الموضع يدل على التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r9.claim: The pronoun هو conveys exclusivity: compared with this ruin, every other loss is as nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r9.anchor: الثالث : أن كلمة ( هو ) : في قوله : { هو الخسران المبين } تفيد الحصر كأنه قيل كل خسران فإنه

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r10.claim: Calling the loss manifest intensifies its terror.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r10.anchor: وصفه بكونه ( مبينا ) : يدل على التهويل

RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r11.claim: Life, intellect, and capacity are capital given by God; life’s purpose is to acquire the good life of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v26p223/r11.anchor: أنه تعالى أعطى هذه الحياة وأعطى العقل ، وأعطى المكنة وكل ذلك رأس المال ، أما هذه الحياة فالمقصود منها أن يكتسب فيها الحياة الطيبة في الآخرة

ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r2.claim: Worship what you will besides God is a threat, like the command to enjoy disbelief briefly; the wording indicates this preceded the command to fight.
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r2.anchor:
هذا على ما قلنا من الوعيد مثل قوله: (قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا).
وهذا يدل - والله أعلم - على أنه قبل أن يؤمر المسلمون بالحرب

ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r3.claim: The passage contrasts the believers' abundant reward with the disbelievers' severe punishment.
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r3.anchor: وقد بين حظ المؤمنين من جزيل الثواب، وحظ الكافرين من عظيم العقاب

ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r4.claim: The losers are the unbelievers: they lose themselves through eternal residence in Hell and their families because they miss the believing families in Paradise.
ZAJJAJ:v4p348/r4.anchor:
هذا يعني به الكفار، فإنهم خسروا أنفسهم بالتخليد في النار، وخسروا
أهليهم

BAQILLANI:v1p86/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p86/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p86/r1.claim: Jinas can be formed by adding or dropping a letter, or through near-similar forms; he illustrates the device with lines from al-Buhturi, Ibn Muqbil, Zuhayr, Abu Tammam, Abu Nuwas, Ibn al-Mu'tazz, and al-Mutanabbi.

BAQILLANI:v1p86/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p86/r2.claim: Some count Qur'anic wording among this kind of wordplay, including the paired forms in the challenge not to hasten and the contrast between declaring worship of God and telling others to worship as they wish.
BAQILLANI:v1p86/r2.anchor: وقد قيل إن من هذا القبيل قوله عز وجل
